en: The Apadāna of the Elder Aññāsikoṇḍañña Buddhavagga 9 I was a young brahmin, well-versed in the Vedas, living at the foot of a tree in the forest. At that time, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One named Dīpaṅkara, appeared in the world. Accompanied by a great assembly of monks, he traveled from village to village, from town to town. Having arrived at the city of Ramma, he took up residence there. Hearing that the Blessed One had arrived, the people of Ramma prepared a great festival. On the day of the festival, I too went to the city of Ramma. There, amidst the great crowd, I saw the Teacher, the Blessed One, seated upon his throne. With palms joined in reverence, I paid homage to him. Then, having offered a handful of lotuses to the Blessed One, I made this aspiration: "May I, through this root of merit, become a disciple of this very Buddha. At that moment, the Great Sage, the Knower of the World, knowing my aspiration, prophesied: "Young man, you shall indeed become a disciple of this very Buddha. Having heard those words of the Great Sage, I was filled with joy and delight. Then, with a mind full of faith, I departed from that place. In the final existence, I was born in a wealthy family. Having renounced the world under the dispensation of Kassapa, the Fully Enlightened One, I practiced the holy life. Having fulfilled the perfections, I have now attained the supreme state of peace. Through the power of that former aspiration, I have realized the goal. Thus did I speak these verses concerning my own past deeds. May all beings attain happiness. May there be well-being for all. “To the Fully Enlightened One Padumuttara,
the eldest in the world, the Leader,
who has reached the plane of Buddhahood— ”
This was the first thing I saw:
all the yakkhas who had gathered at the foot of the Bodhi tree.
Surrounding the Fully Awakened One,
they pay homage with palms joined;
all the gods are joyful in mind.
They move through the sky;
this Buddha has arrived,
the dispeller of the darkness of gloom.
As they were overcome with laughter, a great cry arose:
"We shall burn away our defilements!"
In the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
having understood the speech of the devas,
I uttered this lion’s roar.
Joyful, with a joyful heart,
I gave the first alms; having understood my intention,
[the Blessed One accepted it].
The Teacher, unsurpassed in the world,
sat amidst the assembly of devas and spoke these verses.
Having gone forth for seven days,
I attained enlightenment;
this was my first meal.
It was for the sustenance of the one living the holy life.
For it was the Tusita devas who, having come here,
brought almsfood to me.
I shall proclaim his praise;
listen as I speak.
For thirty thousand aeons,
He will exercise sovereignty over the gods;
having surpassed all the gods,
he will dwell in the triple heaven.
Having passed away from the deva-worlds,
he will go to the human state as a wheel-turning monarch with a thousandfold power.
There he will exercise sovereignty.
In a hundred thousand aeons,
born of the Okkāka clan;
One named Gotama by clan will become a teacher in the world;
having passed away from the Tidasas, he—
He will attain human birth;
having gone forth from the home,
he will dwell for six years.
“Then, in the seventh year,
the Buddha will proclaim the Truth;
he who is known by the name Koṇḍañña.”
‘I shall realize it first.
Having gone forth following him who had departed,
I accomplished my striving well.
For the sake of burning away the defilements,
I went forth into the homeless life.
Having approached the All-Knowing One,
In the world with its devas, the Buddha,
in the Deer Park at Isipatana,
beat the drum of the Deathless.
Thus now he has attained the deathless,
the unsurpassed state of peace,
having fully understood all taints.
I dwell free from taints.
The four analytical knowledges and these eight liberations—
"The six direct knowledges have been realized;
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the elder venerable Aññāsikoṇḍañña speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Aññāsikoṇḍañña is the seventh.
